facts.text: Commodore Oliver Hazard Perry led a victorious squadron at the historic Battle of Lake Erie, cementing the city’s naval legacy.
Erie grew into a mid‑19th‑century hub for shipbuilding, fishing, and railroads, fueling its rise as a Great Lakes powerhouse.
The French built Fort‑Presque‑Isle on Erie’s mainland in 1753, the last French post west of the Niagara River before the war.
Since the 1980s, the International Institute of Erie has welcomed refugees from over a dozen countries, enriching the city’s cultural tapestry.
Erie’s historic Warner Theatre, downtown, continues to host a wide range of performances, echoing its 1920s grandeur.
The city once boasted distinct ethnic enclaves, such as Little Italy on West 18th Street, reflecting its diverse immigrant roots.
